##### **Improvements to your** **_Copper Monitor_** 

Dear Subscriber, 

We are pleased to announce a number of enhancements to the **quality** and **consistency** of data and presentation of content across CRU’s LME metal Monitors.  This will take place from the September publication the _Copper Monitor_ . 

We are making these enhancements in response to subscriber feedback, and they are intended to improve your experience of analysing CRU data across single or multiple LME commodity markets. 

We understand that changes to our data structure and the layout of tables can impact your work flow so if you have any queries, feedback or concerns please do not hesitate to contact us. 

Yours sincerely, 

##### **Vanessa Davidson** 



##### **Peter Ghilchik**

#### Prices stabilise amid quiet market conditions 

- LME copper prices stabilised in July, trading within a relatively narrow range of $7,400-7,800/t. Similarly to previous months, fluctuations in price have been determined largely by macroeconomic events rather than by developments in copper market fundamentals. 

- Physical buying activity is extremely quiet at present; the inactivity exacerbated by the onset of the summer holiday

period in the northern hemisphere. Spot demand is described as virtually nonexistent and supply is adequate to meet limited requests for spot material. - Despite weak demand, the ingredients for the reappearance of a tight market in September remain in place. Forecast production allows for potential disruptions and feasible raw material balances. © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** Copper Monitor August 2012 www.crugroup.com #### Prices range-bound in quiet market Following the sharp decline in May and June, LME copper prices traded sideways in July within a relatively narrow range of $7,400-7,800/t. Similarly to previous months, fluctuations in price have been determined largely by macroeconomic events rather than by developments in copper market fundamentals. Trade and speculator selling, in response to the release of weak economic data, has persisted over the last month but periodic bouts of short-covering have ensured that downward price momentum has been limited. Many traders and investors, however, remain absent from the ma

rket, waiting for signs that policy makers in Europe, the USA and China will commit to new stimulus measures in an effort to support economic growth in the second half of the year. Signs, though, are not overwhelmingly positive. During the latest US Federal Reserve meeting, it was acknowledged that additional bond buying could be on the agenda to bolster the sluggish US economy but no specific plans were announced. Attention is now focussed on the imminent ECB meeting in which it is hoped that fresh measures to support the Eurozone will be revealed. Statements from ECB president, Mario Draghi, claiming he intends to do whatever is necessary to save the euro, has generated optimism and there is scope for copper prices to rally should sufficient action be agreed. There have also been positive comments from Chinese government officials stating that interest rate cuts will continue during the remainder of the year in order to support Chinese growth. Despite upbeat announcements, the release of Chinese, European and US manufacturing data for July has been met with disappointment and copper prices have subsequently softened. In China, the official factory purchasing managers index fell to an eight-month low of 50.1, while the Eurozone manufacturing sector contracted for the eleventh consecutive month and US manufacturing grew at its slowest Forward curve has similar shape to that in early June pace in nearly three years. Forward curve has similar shape to that in early June LME forward curve, cash=100, Jan 12–Jul 12 But it is not just weak economic data that is limiting the upward potential for copper prices at present. The physical copper market is also extremely quiet; the inactivity exacerbated by the onset of the summer holiday period in the northern hemisphere. Spot demand is virtually non-existent in the key consuming regions and supply is adequate to meet limited spot requests for material. Reflecting the lack of buying interest and limited pressure on supply, the tightness in the forward spreads, which was prevalent a month ago, has faded. A further signal that market conditions have eased is evidence that the dominant warrant holder of a month ago is now holding only 40-50% of stocks in LME warehouses, compared with 50-80% at one stage in June. #### Stocks are low and set to fall further While market activity is subdued for now, all the ingredients for the reappearance o

f a tight market in September or October remain in place. In particular, reported stocks of refined copper outside Asia remain low while those in Asia are likely to be readily absorbed assuming the much-anticipated pick-up in Chinese demand materialises in the coming months. In the USA, inventories of copper cathode have continued to decline. Those held in LME warehouses have fallen by 10,000t to a level of 121,200t and Comex stocks have been drawn down by a further 4,800t in recent weeks. Stocks held in LME European warehouses ticked up slightly in July, by 2,300t, but at 16,200t are far from excessive. By contrast, stocks in Asian warehouses are described as ample. SHFE inventories increased by 17,100t in July and there was a 50,000t increase in Chinese bonded warehouse stocks to a level of 550,000t. Following the influx of copper into Asian LME warehouses in June, stocks remained unchanged in July. However, data for cancelled LME warrants, an indicator of upcoming withdrawals of copper from LME warehouses, are once again running at high levels, with the majority associated with the Korean warehouses of Busan and Gwangyang. From just 26,600t at the end of June, total cancelled warrants reached a high of 56,100t in mid-July and were still at elevated levels of 48,900t by the end of the month. #### Contract business solid in USA and Europe Despite limited activity in the spot markets of North America and Europe, contract business is described as solid. Customers in both regions are continuing to take contracted volumes of refined copper with no evidence of cancellations or postponements beyond normal levels. True, volumes are comparatively low but this partly reflects closures among semi-fabricators for summer maintenance purposes. There also continue to be regional variations in demand, with European offtake described as the weakest, due to heavy ongoing destocking in the region, and US buying activity slightly better. In the USA, the automotive sector is continuing to perform well, with Ford and Chrysler reporting that they’ll limit summer shutdowns at their plants in order to meet demand for new vehicles, but the © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 18 Copper Monitor August 2012 www.crugroup.com construction sector remains weak. Within Europe there is evidence that countries in the north of the region are experiencing better demand than those in the south but, given the current overall weaknesses of the banking system in the EU, end-users across the spectrum are suffering a credit squeeze. #### Chinese demand leading the way Chinese buying activity softened further in July co

mpared with June, as the expected seasonal upturn in demand failed to emerge. Some market participants point to the 17.5% month-on-month fall in imports of unwrought copper in June as confirmation of demand weakness. But imports had been running at such high levels in previous months that it was always Chinese imports expected to likely that such volumes would be difficult to come down further maintain. In our view, underlying consumption of refined copper in China is stronger than appears at first sight. Shortages of scrap in the country are forcing semi-fabricators to use a greater proportion of refined copper in place of secondary material. Since China is heavily dependent on imports for its supplies of scrap, it has been the negative SHFE/LME arbitrage combined with stronger US demand that have been the key factors behind the reduction in Chinese scrap availability in recent months. #### Premiums holding up in most regions The lack of spot business in all regions makes it difficult to accurately assess merchant premiums. On balance, market participants report that European premiums have weakened over the last month but the absence of a significant number of deals suggests that quotes are more nominal in nature than actual. Those for good quality cathode are understood to have dropped on average by $10/t to around $60-80/t cif Rotterdam. However, delays to some vessels from Chile in mid-July saw premiums rise temporarily to as much as $90-100/t. In the USA, where premiums had previously been increasing in response to the drawdown in exchange stocks, there is evidence that premiums have stabilised. Traders are quoting levels of 7.0-8.0¢/lb, delivered east coast, which are unchanged from June. Despite weak buying interest, rising stocks and bearish sentiment, the Chinese market is nevertheless displaying some signs of strength. China’s spot import premium, cif Shanghai basis, moved up a notch in July to $70-80/t. This suggests excess supply is not being viewed as overly significant, although this © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 4 of 18 Copper Monitor August 2012 www. crugroup.com could change if buying activity remains subdued. For now, opinions are divided. Some insiders foresee copper demand improving, boosted by further interest rate cuts and expectations of the government doubling railway investment. Others, m

eanwhile, are sceptical that the government’s economic stimuli will be sufficient to offset the general frailty of the economy. #### Supply underperformance keeps market tight Disruptions to existing mine and smelter production coupled with delays to new mines are a key factor behind our view that the copper market has experienced a sizeable deficit in the year to date. Though second quarter global mine output is believed to have increased quarter-on-quarter, up by 6.3%, there continue to be reports of operations struggling to hit targets. Mine output at Collahuasi, for example, was down heavily in the second quarter as well as the first, while output at Grasberg has yet to return to normal levels, following the end to the strike last year. Additionally, the latest financial results from Rio Tinto point to substantial declines at mine output at Kennecott in both the first and second quarters. Even in the face of these ongoing issues, the market is watching mine developments carefully for signs that supply will start to increase on a more consistent basis. There has been strong growth in mine production at Escondida this year, as a result of higher ore grades, and there are 25 new mines scheduled to start-up in the second half of 2012. Nevertheless, market participants remain unconvinced that output will increase significantly this year and suspect that disruptions and delays will remain widespread. #### Waiting for direction LME copper prices appear well supported in their current trading range, requiring a fresh catalyst to enable them to break out on either the upside or the downside. While it is doubtful that such an incentive will appear over the summer, it is likely the market will move more decisively in September. Should Chinese demand start to improve, the US recovery pick-up pace and an end to European destocking boost buying activity in the region, the copper market could tighten quickly, especially as stocks remain low. It is also likely that greater certainty over the future direction of the euro could encourage funds back into the market. For now, investors remain firmly on the sidelines hoping to avoid a situation in which price gains in commodities are eliminated by a stronger US dollar. Most recently in Q2 2012, wirerod consumption was up by a mere 1.1% y-o-y. This compares poorly to the rate of growth seen in global industrial production, which accelerated to go above 5% y- o-y in Q2. We attribute most of this divergence to weakness in the construction sector, which is not included as a part of the industrial production index. World wirerod demand growth

The slowing trend is reflected in most of the **-10%** world’s largest wirerod markets. China’s growth momentum cooled as wirerod demand rose by **-15%** only 2.3% y-o-y, much slower than the 7.1% y- o-y growth seen in Q1. China accounts for 60% **-20%** IP, %y-o-y Wirerod consumption, %y-o-y chg of the global market, making any change **Data: CRU** significant to the world picture. However, the USA, South Korea, Taiwan and Germany, accounting for 18% of the world’s consumption of wirerod, also exhibited significantly weakened y-o-y growth than in Q1. China’s slowdown has been the result of weaker than usual private consumption following the Chinese Spring and Lantern festivals in Q1 due to the government’s restraints on new private housing construction. This has also impacted sales of domestic appliances and associated electrical engineering sectors. In addition, there has been a significant build of stocks down the value chain, as the result of weaker than expected retail sales in Q1. This has slowed wirerod consumption for low voltage energy and winding wire production, as the supply chain de-stocks. Furthermore, investment expenditure from the power industry seems to be materialising more slowly than expected. The South Korean and Taiwanese markets both suffered y-o-y contractions in wirerod demand in Q2: a loss totalling 19,000t. In the case of Korea, which saw a decline in wirerod consumption of 7% y-o-y to reach 135,000t in Q2, the **Korean Statistical Information Service** informs us that the economy shrank in several key end-use sectors for wirerod in Q2 2012. Construction activity, in value terms (constant prices), fell by 10% y-o-y and total orders for motors (excl. those for transport), motor vehicles and electrical machinery fell by 22%, 12% and 12% y-o-y, respectively. These sectors impact wirerod consumption via weakness in the low voltage energy cable and winding wire segments, whose aggregate production we see falling by around 5% y-o-y in 2012 in Korea. Likewise, Taiwan also encountered a © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** P

age 10 of 18 Copper Monitor August 2012 www. crugroup.com drop in wirerod consumption in Q2, as volumes decreased by 10% y-o-y (reduction of 8,000t). This fits in with our wire and cable 2012 forecasts’ where we foresee low voltage energy cable and winding wire production falling by 5% y-o-y in full year 2012. Exports of these products are in decline. Whereas, domestic end use indicators from the **Ministry of Economic Affairs** suggest that construction activity was up by 1.4% y-o-y, as were electronic parts and components production, which increased by the same 1.4% y-o-y in Q2. However, smaller segments such as ‘computers, electronic and optical products’ and machinery and equipment, fell by 10% y-o-y and 11.5% y-o-y, respectively. After extraordinary growth in 2011 in the face of European economic uncertainty, Germany’s wirerod demand consolidated at year-ago levels of 140,000t in Q2 2012. Passenger vehicle production, which had been supporting German wirerod demand growth in 2011, could not sustain the same rate in Q2 2012, dropping by 10% y-o-y. Construction figures from **Statistisches Bundesamt** , showed tremendous growth in 2011, as residential and commercial housing permits (including renovations) boasted doubledigit y-o-y growth rates for nine of the twelve months. However, permit issuance took a sharp turn in January, marking the start of four consecutive months of y-o-y contractions. Meanwhile, the home appliance sector has performed relatively better, supporting winding wire and low voltage energy cabling demand. **Zentralverband Elektrotechnik und Elektronikindustrie eV** (the German electrical and electronic equipment manufacturer association) reported a rise of 5% y-o-y in H1 2012 sales in Germany, adding that Q2 demand had slowed, but remained positive. #### US autos no longer fueling US wirerod demand growth? North America represents 11% of the global wirerod market, of which, the USA accounts for 75%. Recently, despite evidence of positive growth in the US construction and automotive sectors, wirerod consumption did not respond in the same way and growth appears to have flatlined in Q2 2012. We attribute this to large wirerod production increases in Mexico as **Grupo Mexico** ’s, **La Caridad** integrated smelter and rod mill, significantly increased its rod plant utilisa

tion rate in 2011 after the restart of the **Buenavista** mine and hence an increase in its dedicated raw material supply. This additional rod output has not been exported and it appears to have been consumed in the production of auto © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 11 of 18 Copper Monitor August 2012 www.crugroup.com wire for vehicle wire harness assembly. One of the key players in this industry in Mexico is **Grupo Carso S.A.B. de C.V.** . Its Q2 2012 report reveals that revenues associated with the products for the automotive sector grew by 8.4% y-o-y in Q2 and 14.4% y-o-y in H1 2012. The change in terms of volume is likely to be even more pronounced as the copper price decreased over this period. However, this year there has been a large acceleration in semi-fabricators output as H1 2012 saw the industry’s production level grow by 18.4% y-o-y. This has been the result of a change in the government’s previous interventionist policies to tighten monetary policy in order to rein in inflation.

Unfortunately, this tightened credit availability for semi-fabricators, who then struggled to source loans for raw materials and had to pay prohibitively high interest rates on working capital.  Now, however, the inflation rate has declined significantly, reaching 4.9% for the year-

### Industry News 

#### Consumption 

- **Jingcheng Copper** announced that it expects to see a loss in H1 2012, citing weak demand and poor utilisation rates at its new flat rolled copper plant in Wuhu City in the Anhui province. Jingcheng Copper produces copper-alloy sheet and strip for domestic and overseas markets.  The company anticipates a 70-90% y-o-y fall in its net profits during H1 2012.  This follows news in early January of the successful commissioning of Jincheng’s new 30,000t/y copper-alloy sheet and strip plant. 

- **Furukawa Electric** said it plans to double sales to around ¥50 billion ($630.7 million) by 2015 though increasing production and sales in Indonesia.  Sales are to increase at the local plant **TMS** which manufactures copper and aluminium wirerod and the company hopes to capture the demand in infrastructure to increase its sales of cables.  The company also expects increased demand from the automobile sector which will have a positive impact on wire harness production.  In addition, Furukawa Electric said it had made an agreement with **SUCACO** for technical assistance with aluminium overhead ground wires and high performance electric wires. 

- **Nexans** said it has been awarded contracts worth around €110M ($113.2 million) by Libya's **PEWCO** (Public Electrical Works Company), to supply cables for projects to upgrade the country's power transmission and distribution infrastructure.  The contracts involve the supply of over 1,000 km of high-voltage (HV) and low and medium-voltage (MV) cables.  The transmission contract comprises 245 kV underground cables to be manufactured and supplied by **Nexans France** and the 33 kV and 15 kV distribution cables and the optical fibre cables being supplied by **Nexans Greece** , with additional accessories being supplied by **Nexans Italy** . Delivery and installation of the cable is expected to be complete by the end of 2013. 

- **Fujikura Ltd.** has announced its plans to build automotive wire harnesses plants in Morocco and Paraguay by the spring of 2013. The company said this will increase the number of personnel by about 3,000 in total in the medium term.  This follows increased demand from Europe and the growing markets in South America.  The new sites have the benefits of lower production costs and being situated near growing markets. 

- Shipments of copper wire and cable from **Japan** increased for the second consecutive month in June, reaching 57,300t.  This represents a 1.0% increase y-o-y and

an 8.0% increase m-o-m. Shipments to the automotive sector performed particularly well, increasing 36.3% y-o-y, following the introduction of subsidies for the purchase of fuel-efficient cars.  Additionally, reconstruction efforts from last year's earthquake and tsunami disaster continue to support demand.

#### Mine Production 

- Kazakh miner **ENRC** has acquired a licence to operate the **Frontier** mine in the DRC in a deal worth US101.5M.  Frontier was operated by **First Quantum** until two years ago when it was confiscated by the government.  ENRC’s involvement in the DRC has been surrounded by some controversy; two years ago, ENRC bought the **Kolwezi** operation in the DRC that had also previously been expropriated by the government from First Quantum.  A legal battle with First Quantum ensued.  The parties reached a settlement in January 2012, with ENRC agreeing to pay US$1.25B for Kolwezi and purchase First Quantum’s other operations in the DRC, which included the **Longi** and Frontier operations.  The deal did not include mining licences. 

- On 25<sup>th</sup> July, the Zambian government announced that it plans to increase its ownership stake in mining operations in the country to as much as 25%.  However, it is unclear whether this will apply to all mining operations.  Mines Minister Christopher Yaluma said: “We don’t have any intentions to raise our ownership in most of the mining houses.“  Earlier announcements by the **Ministry of Mines** suggested that the government was seeking to gain 35% ownership of mining operations, but this plan was abandoned.  The Zambian government currently holds a 10-20% stake in most mining operations in the country through **ZCCM Investment Holdings Plc** . 

- **Freeport McMoRan** announced that it is offering a 9.4% stake in **PT Freeport Indonesia** , the operator of the **Grasberg** mine, to the regional government in Papua, where the mine is located. According to Freeport, the stake was initially offered to the central government who then reoffered it to the local administration. 

- Contract workers at **Codelco** ’s **Chuquicamata** mine in Chile staged a strike on 19<sup>th</sup> July. The striking workers, hired by subcontractor **Metalcav** , demanded higher wages and better bonuses. Road blocks were erected at the mine by protesters, however, according to Codelco, there were no disruptions to production.  In 2011, the Chuquicamata mine produced over 430,000t of contained copper, and is expected to produce in excess of 380,000t this year. 

- Violent protests continue against **Newmont’s Conga** copper-gold project in Peru.  It was reported on July 5<sup>th</sup> that 5 people had been killed during clashes with police and a state of emergency was declared.  This latest round of protests has been underway for a month.  In late June, Newmont announced that it would revise t

he project and remove two, not four, mountain lakes and replace them with reservoirs.  This work will be done in advance of the mine construction in a bid to reduce the local opposition to the project. 

- On 17<sup>th</sup> July, **First Quantum Minerals** announced that it had halted production at its **Guelb Moghrein** copper and gold mine in Mauritania after mine workers went on strike over pay and violent clashe broke out between the striking workers and police, leaving one worker dead.  First Quantum is currently in talks with the unions in a government mediated negotiation process. Although, an agreement has yet to be reached, workers began to return to work on 27<sup>th</sup> July.

#### Exploration and Development 

- On 17<sup>th</sup> July, it was announced that stakeholders of **Anglo American** ’s **Quellaveco** project have given the go-ahead for the project’s development. The project is located in southern Peru and was privatised almost 20 years ago. An Environmental Impact Assessment was initially approved for the development in 2000 (with some later amendments), but was eventually blocked due to opposition from the local population.  Last, week, after 18 months of negotiations, the stakeholders finally reached an agreement.  Anglo American agreed to contribute US$370M to local developments over the 30-year mine life. Construction of the 225,000t/y copper-in-concentrate project could begin next year, with start-up in 2016. The investment has been estimated at US$3.0B, although the final capex has not been approved. 

- On 28<sup>th</sup> July, it was reported that **BHP Billiton** is likely to delay a decision on a US$30B investment in the expansion of the **Olympic Dam** mine in South Australia.  The original plan for the mine included a 5-stage development strategy in the period until 2020.  The first stage has already b

een completed and the second stage was planned to be completed by 2016.  While BHP Billiton has not made any official statements, reports suggest that the decision of whether or not to proceed with the expansion will be deferred to 2014.  The state government has set a deadline for BHP Billiton to approve the investment by the end of the year if the company wants to avoid having to renegotiate all government approvals.  Olympic Dam is expected to produce 206,000t of contained copper in 2012. 

- On 31<sup>st</sup> July, **Xstrata** announced that mining operations had begun at the **Mount Margaret** mine, located near Cloncurry in North-West Queensland, Australia.  The mine is expected to produce 30,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate over the 5 year mine life.  In addition to copper, the mine will also produce 110,000t/y of iron ore and 17,000oz of gold annually.  The ore from the mine will be trucked to Xstrata’s **Ernest Henry** operation where it will be processed at the existing copper concentrator and iron ore plant.  Xstrata also plans to carry out further exploration activity at Mount Margaret to identify additional ore resources.

#### Smelting and Refining 

- On 30<sup>th</sup> July **, Jiangxi Copper Company Ltd** announced that it plans to invest 8B Yuan (US$1.25B) to build new smelting and refining capacity in the Zhejiand province in China.  The company plans to partner with **Fuchunjiang Smelting** , to create **Zhejiang Heding Copper** that will manage the construction and operation of the project.  The new operation aims to have a smelting capacity of 200,000t/y of copper-in-blister and 370,000t/y of copper cathode. **Jiangxi Copper Company Ltd** is currently also working with **Yantai Penghui Copper Industry** to build a 300,000t/y smelter in the Shandong province. 

- **Codelco** announced on 19<sup>th</sup> July that it plans to invest US$300M to improve sulphur capture at its **El Teniente** smelter.  Chilean law stipulates that smelters are required to capture 95% of sulphur emissions and the El Teniente smelter currently captures only around 93%.  This step is part of a more general US$1B investment project by Codelco to improve the environmental standards at all its operations. 

- On 31<sup>st</sup> July, the **Zambian Environmental Management Agency** (ZEMA) announced that it had received an application for an environmental permit for **First Quantum Minerals** ’ new smelter project in Zambia.  Construction of the new smelter is expected to cost US$460M, and it has a planned production capacity of 300,000t of copper-in-blister.  The new smelter will be located in the Solwezi district, on land already under First Quantum’s mining license for the Kansanshi mine.
